heading: Secure inter-site communication with custom certificates
abstract: By default, the Skupper controller generates internal Certificate Authorities (CAs) and self-signed certificates. For example, it creates certificates to authenticate incoming Skupper links from external Skupper sites.

heading: Migrate from {skupper_name} v1
abstract: {skupper_name} v1 sites are not compatible with {skupper_name} v2 sites. While there are plans to create migration tooling, currently, the only way migrate an application network is to create a new network.

heading: Establish system connectivity

heading: Create a Kubernetes connector using the CLI

heading: Link sites using a `link` resource
abstract: An alternative approach to linking sites using tokens is to create a `link` resource YAML file using the CLI, and to apply that resource to another site.

heading: Specify link cost using the CLI
abstract: Link cost is a configurable integer value that influences how Skupper routes traffic across links between sites. The routing algorithm favors paths with the lowest total cost from client to target server.

heading: Link sites through an HTTP proxy
abstract: If your network requires routing through an HTTP CONNECT proxy to reach remote sites, you can configure Skupper links to use a proxy. This feature is only available when using `link` resources, not tokens.

heading: Link sites using a token
abstract: A token provides a secure method to link sites. By default, a token can only be used once and must be used within 15 minutes to link sites. Issue a token from one site and redeem that token on another site to create a link.

heading: Link sites using `AccessGrant` and `AccessToken` resources

heading: Create a Kubernetes listener using YAML
abstract: A listener binds a local connection endpoint to connectors in remote sites. Listeners and connectors are matched using routing keys.

heading: Create a Kubernetes multi-key listener using YAML
abstract: A multi-key listener binds a single local host and port to multiple routing keys in remote sites. Use a multi-key listener when you want one service endpoint to aggregate traffic from multiple connectors.

heading: Link sites using a custom `RouterAccess`, and custom certificates
abstract: By default, when you set `spec.linkAccess` on a `Site`, the Skupper controller automatically creates a `RouterAccess` named `skupper-router` with `generateTlsCredentials: true` and `tlsCredentials: skupper-site-server`.

heading: Custom certificates and YAML
